title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
Overview

This playbook describes Redwood Inference’s standard approach to on-call and incident response: severity definitions, triage and escalation flows, runbook patterns, postmortem process, rotation rules, game-day guidance, and customer-facing status updates. The goal is to restore service quickly, communicate clearly to stakeholders and customers, and capture learnings to prevent recurrence.

Scope

- Applies to all production-facing services owned or operated by Redwood Inference (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployments support plane, monitoring & alerting).
- Includes detection, triage, mitigation, escalation, communication, and post-incident analysis.

Key roles and responsibilities

- Pager (Primary Oncall): First responder responsible for initial triage and mitigation.
- Secondary (Backup Oncall): Assists primary, takes over if primary unavailable or incident scales.
- L2 / Service Owner: Engineer(s) with deep knowledge of the affected service responsible for root cause analysis and longer-term mitigation.
- Incident Commander (IC): Appointed for SEV1+ incidents to coordinate cross-team response, communications, and postmortem ownership.
- Communications Lead: Owns status page, customer and internal comms.
- Postmortem Owner: Owns the writeup, action items, and tracking.

Severity definitions and expected timelines

- SEV0 (critical outage): Complete service outage or major data-loss affecting customers. Target: 15 minute acknowledgment, 60 minute initial mitigation plan, 4 hour resolution expectation.
- SEV1 (service degradation): Severe degradation (high error rate, long tail latency) impacting large portion of customers. Target: 30 minute acknowledgment, 90 minute mitigation window.
- SEV2 (partial impact): Functional regression affecting subset of users or non-critical features. Target: 60 minute acknowledgment, mitigation in next business day if not customer-facing.
- SEV3 (informational): Alerts requiring operational attention or improvement (metrics trending). Target: acknowledge within one business day.

Incident lifecycle (standard steps)

1) Detection and Alerting
- Alerts originate from Prometheus/Sensu/Datadog synthetic tests, customer reports, or monitoring jobs.
- Alerts must include: affected service, symptom, key metrics (error rate, p95 latency, availability), dashboard link, and runbook link.

2) Acknowledgement and Triage
- The oncall engineer acknowledges the alert within the severity SLA.
- Quick checks: telemetry dashboard, recent deploys, infra events, incident tracker (PagerDuty), and traffic change.
- Determine severity, impact, and whether to call Incident Commander.

3) Mitigation and Short-term Remediation
- Execute relevant runbook steps. Actions may include traffic shaping, config rollback, scaling, throttling, or failover to a compatible model variant.
- Document each action in the incident timeline (start time, actor, outcome).

4) Escalation and Coordination
- If mitigation is not effective within the timeframe, escalate to L2 and the IC.
- IC opens a dedicated incident bridge (Zoom/Slack Huddle) and assigns a Communications Lead.

5) Customer and Internal Communications
- Post an initial status update within the SLA window (15–60 minutes depending on severity).
- Use the templates below for status page and email/slack communications.

6) Resolution and Recovery
- Confirm service health via telemetry for the defined SLO thresholds for at least two consecutive observation windows.
- If a rollback was used, coordinate to re-deploy a validated fix with the release owner.

7) Postmortem and Remediation
- For SEV1/SEV0 and significant SEV2 incidents, create a postmortem within 72 hours and a final writeup within 7 days. Include timeline, root cause, customer impact, and action items.

Runbook templates (structure and examples)

Each runbook should follow this template: 
- Title
- Purpose and scope
- Owner and escalation path
- Detection criteria and key dashboards
- Pre-checks (before taking action)
- Step-by-step mitigation steps (ordered, with CLI/console commands where applicable)
- Verification steps (metrics and dashboards to confirm resolution)
- Rollback and post-incident actions
- Related pages and playbooks

Example: API High 5xx Rate (runbook)
- Purpose: Recover from sudden spike in 5xx responses on the hosted inference API.
- Owner: api-team@redwood.com
- Detection: 5xx rate > 2% for 5 minute window or p95 latency > 2s above baseline. Dashboard: /dashboards/hosted-api-ops
- Pre-checks: confirm recent deploys (last 60m), infra alerts, and queue backpressure metrics.
- Mitigation steps: 
  1) Isolate the region: route new traffic to unaffected regions using traffic routing UI (owner: infra-oncall).
  2) Disable new model rollouts via feature-flag in Console.
  3) Scale up inference pool (if autoscaling failing) using infra playbook: kubectl scale or autoscaler override.
  4) If error source is model-worker, perform graceful restart of worker group with rolling restarts (max 10% concurrency).
  5) If latency persists, shift traffic to lower-cost model variant as fallback.
- Verification: error rate <0.5% and p95 latency within 10% of baseline for 10 minutes.
- Rollback & Post-incident: if root cause is a deploy, rollback to previous artifact and trigger gated redeploy after fix.

Example: Model KV-cache Corruption (runbook)
- Detection: increased wrong-token predictions and KV-miss spikes.
- Mitigation: disable cache warmup, purge KV cache for affected partitions, throttle new session creation.
- Verification: prediction accuracy and KV hit-rate return to expected range.

On-call rotations and schedules

- Rotation model: weekly rotation for primary oncall; secondary oncall is the following engineer for the same week. L2 owners maintain monthly on-call schedules.
- Shift handoff: a 15-minute asynchronous handoff document is required in Slack #oncall-handoff at shift start describing ongoing incidents, ongoing mitigations, and any maintenance windows.
- Escalation timeline: primary (10 min) -> secondary (20 min) -> L2/service-owner (30–60 min) -> IC (if unresolved).
- Tools: PagerDuty for paging and escalations; Slack for bridge and IC coordination; StatusPage for public updates.

Game days and preparedness exercises

- Frequency: quarterly cross-team game days and one annual full-scale simulation.
- Objectives: validate alert fidelity, exercise runbooks and escalation paths, rehearse customer comms, and surface gaps in tooling or telemetry.
- Scenarios: region outage, high latency under load, degraded model quality, and control-plane failover.
- Post-game-day: formal report with action items tracked in the incident retrospective board.

Status page and customer communications templates

Guiding principles
- Be timely: publish an initial status update within the severity SLA window.
- Be brief and factual: state impact, scope, and next steps.
- Avoid speculation: only include verified facts.
- Provide cadence: publish updates at regular intervals (every 30–60 minutes for SEV0/SEV1).

Initial public status update (template)
- Title: [Service] — Degraded Performance (Region)
- Body: We are investigating elevated error rates affecting the [service name] in [region]. Some customers may experience increased latency or errors. Our oncall team is actively investigating. We will post updates every 30 minutes. (Impact: % of requests affected / Affected features: e.g., generation API).

Customer acknowledgement email (template)
- Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident Acknowledgement for [Service] on [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Body: Hello — We detected an issue affecting [service]. We have acknowledged the incident and are actively working on remediation. We will share periodic updates and a post-incident report when available. If you have specific questions about data integrity or compliance, please reply to this email and include your account ID.

Status update example (follow-up)
- Title: [Service] — Partial Recovery (Region)
- Body: We have implemented mitigation steps that reduced error rates and restored service capacity for most traffic. A subset of customers may still see intermittent errors. Our engineers are continuing remediation and validation. Estimated next update: in 60 minutes.

Incident resolution and postmortem process

- Postmortem required for all SEV0/SEV1 incidents and SEV2 incidents that meet impact thresholds (customer-reported SLA breach, data loss, or extended downtime).
- Template fields (postmortem): 
  - Title
  - Summary (one-paragraph impact & status)
  - Severity
  - Detection time, mitigation time, resolution time
  - Root cause (concise)
  - Timeline (chronological bullet list of actions with timestamps)
  - Impact (customers, SLOs, telemetry)
  - Corrective and preventative actions (ACTIONS with owners and due dates)
  - Follow-up review date

- Postmortem ownership: IC appoints Postmortem Owner during incident. Owner publishes a draft to the incident board within 72 hours and a final version within 7 days. Action items must be tracked in the engineering backlog with labels "incident-action" and assigned owners.

Reporting and metrics

- Every incident entry must include: PagerDuty incident ID, affected services, severity, detected_at, mitigated_at, resolved_at, incident owner, and postmortem link.
- Team-level monthly incident report should summarize incidents, trends, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), MTTR, and outstanding action items.

Related playbooks and links

- Runbook repository: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks

Appendix: Quick reference commands and dashboards

- Dashboards: Hosted API ops (/dashboards/hosted-api-ops), Model serving health (/dashboards/model-serving-health), KV cache metrics (/dashboards/kv-cache)
- Common commands: 
  - kubectl get pods -n inference
  - kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-worker --namespace=inference
  - redis-cli -h kv-cache-host INFO
  - aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name <group> --desired-capacity <n>

Contact and escalation directory

- PagerDuty primary: oncall@redwood.pagerduty.com
- Engineering SRE rotation: eng-sre@redwood.com
- Incident Commander escalation channel: #incident-commander (Slack)
